children: *TPG Files Confidential IPO Application for Malaysia Hospitals Valued at Around $8.0B, Sources Say
*TPG Malaysia Hospital Assets IPO Could Raise Up to $2.5B, Sources Say
*TPG Hospital Assets IPO, Listing Could Take Place in Early Jan, Sources Say
*Deal Could Be Malaysia's Third-Largest IPO Ever
*TPG Also Expected to Initiate Sale Process for Same Malaysia Hospital Assets Next Month, Sources Say
TPG Submits Confidential IPO for Malaysia Hospital Assets Valued at Around $8 Billion
By P.R. Venkat
Private-equity firm TPG has filed a confidential application to list hospitals assets valued at close to $8.0 billion in Malaysia, people familiar with the matter said.

The offering could raise as much as $2.5 billion, the people said. If successful, that would be the third-largest deal in Malaysia, behind Petronas Chemicals' $4.14 billion IPO and a $3.1 billion offering by Felda Global Ventures, now known as FGV Holdings.

TPG submitted a preliminary application pack with Malaysia's Securities Commission last week, the people said. The offering and listing could take place in early January, they said, and a preliminary prospectus is expected to be filed with the stock exchange by early November.

As part of a dual-track strategy, TPG is also expected to launch a sale process for the same Malaysia hospital assets, the people said, which are ultimately set to be sold through either a trade sale or an IPO. The sale process may start as early as next month, they said.
The assets involved are Malaysia-based hospitals operated by Asia OneHealthcare, or A1Health, a private healthcare services provider.

In 2019, TPG and Malaysian conglomerate Hong Leong agreed to acquire Columbia Asia Healthcare, now known as A1Health, from Seattle-based Columbia Pacific Management for $1.2 billion. The operator was renamed in 2024 following the consolidation of healthcare assets across Malaysia, Indonesia and Vietnam.

Today, its portfolio includes more than 4,000 hospital beds in Southeast Asia, with the bulk of its hospitals located in Malaysia. A1Health operates 22 hospitals in the country, as well as other facilities.

Deal activity in Asia's medical-services sector has been strong in recent quarters, fueled by rising patient volumes and healthcare spending. A growing middle class and urbanization are creating attractive opportunities for investors to seek a share of the region's most promising hospital and specialty-care assets.
Demand for listings has been encouraging since the start of the year. Hong Kong has led the region in activity, with momentum spilling over into other markets.

Malaysia hosted 60 listings last year--the most in two decades--and the pace has carried on into this year. In the first half of 2026, 36 companies raised a combined $1.34 billion in Malaysia's capital markets. Sunway Healthcare's over $700 million IPO has been the biggest so far.
U.S.-listed TPG is one of the world's largest alternative asset managers, with $327 billion under management as of June 30.
Ying Xian Wong Contributed to the article
